evidence.V1: Top and three-quarter clearly read as a plank floor; front view and silhouette are a plain box with a lid strip, readable as a crate/chest rather than floor at 64 px
evidence.V2: Big plinth and medium planks are clear, but the small level is just two tiny nail heads, both on one plank, so detail is sparse and unevenly placed
evidence.V3: Stiff: four identical full-length 1-stud planks with no staggered butt joints, warp or end variation; the 2-stud plinth is a plain undetailed block
evidence.V4: Planks have consistent soft chamfers that catch light, but the plinth's vertical corners and top edge are hard/unchamfered (close_edge_studio), so treatment is inconsistent
evidence.V5: Clean: no seams, pinches or z-fighting in close_planks/close_edge studio and flat renders; gaps between planks read as designed grooves
evidence.V6: Disciplined: one wood hue in three values (light plank, dark plank, plinth); painted colourways keep the same value structure
evidence.V7: 200 tris vs module target 800 (ceiling 2000): well under target
evidence.V8: Single LF_VertexColor material and wood hue match, T1 tiling passes on 2-stud grid; minor mismatch from the unchamfered plinth and very sparse ink nail accents
evidence.V9: Studio line correct for a modular piece: anchored, Box collision, CanTouch off, grid-corner pivot, Color white, SmoothPlastic

top_fixes: Add staggered plank butt joints / varied plank lengths and a slight per-plank height or end bevel variation so it reads as hand-laid floor
Chamfer the plinth edges (~0.05-0.07 studs) to match the planks, or add a timber edge band so the side view reads as floor not a box
Place ink nail heads consistently at both ends of every plank
